lanes.hillsLocal.note: Eric, 2026-10-31: almost every hill street is two lanes, one each direction. Applied to Local streets in City Fire Zones 2 and 3.

lanes.byClass.note: Total lanes by County CLASS where the City pavement-management lane count is missing.

parking.hills.note: Eric, 2026-10-31: parking on both sides in the hills, applied only where a 10 ft lane remains. The City's curb data (used by KLD) would replace this; SB 99 report notes many Panoramic Hill roads have no street parking (SOURCE_NOTES A7).

parking.flats.note: Placeholder: parking on both sides. Replace with the City's curb data.

parking.parkedCarWidthM.note: 8 ft per parked side, as used by KLD in the SB 99 and AB 747 analyses (SOURCE_NOTES A1).

capacity.speedMph.note: Free-flow speed by road class (hills 20 mph matches AB 747: hills free flow 20 mph or less). Capped by the City network SPEED where known. Replace with KLD's surveyed speeds.

capacity.twoLanePcphPerMph.note: AB 747 Table 2 (HCM 2022): two-lane road capacity = 45 pc/h per mph of free-flow speed, max 1,700 (SOURCE_NOTES B2). Applied per direction.

capacity.multilanePcphPerLane.note: AB 747: 1,900 pc/h per lane for multilane roadways (SOURCE_NOTES B3).

capacity.freewayPcphPerLane.note: AB 747: 2,250 pc/h per lane for freeways at 55 mph (SOURCE_NOTES B3).

capacity.rampPcphPerLane.note: Ramp capacity placeholder; AB 747 uses HCM Exhibit 14-12 by ramp speed.

capacity.steepFactor.note: Flow multiplier on segments whose steep grade (90th percentile of 25 m windows) exceeds steepGradePct. KLD's surveyed speeds would already include grade.

capacity.vehicleSpacingM.note: Road length one queued vehicle occupies (storage).

access.movingLaneM.note: 10 ft minimum viable evacuation travel lane, chosen by KLD with City Public Works and Fire staff (SOURCE_NOTES A2).

access.engineClearM.note: Largest City fire truck is 9.25 ft wide (SB 99 report, SOURCE_NOTES A3); with mirrors it needs the same 10 ft lane.

access.fireCodeClearM.note: 20 ft unobstructed width for fire apparatus access roads, California Fire Code section 503.2.1. Context only: it governs new access roads, not existing streets.

access.engineServiceMin.note: 5-minute fire-station drive-time standard from the City's Standards of Coverage, as used in the SB 99 analysis (SOURCE_NOTES A6).

intersections.note: Total vehicles per hour a node can pass, by the highest road class meeting there. Illustrative. The 2025 study names intersections as the main constraint.

demand.personsPerHousehold.note: 2.37 persons per household (ACS), Evacuation Time Study 2-1, 3-3 (SOURCE_NOTES E5). Converts Genasys zone population estimates to households.

demand.householdsWithoutVehicleShare.note: 7.47% of households have no vehicle (ACS), Time Study Table 3-10 (SOURCE_NOTES E7). Citywide value; AB 747 has it by census tract.

demand.vehiclesTakenShares.note: Of households that drive: 1 vehicle 73.6%, 2 vehicles 14.6%, 3 vehicles 1.3%, 4+ 0.5% (Time Study survey, Fig. D-11), renormalized (SOURCE_NOTES E6).

demand.carlessRideshareShare.note: 86.9% of people without a vehicle ride with someone else (Time Study 3-9). In the game they ride with an evacuating household on the same street; the rest are stranded (SOURCE_NOTES E7).

demand.compliance.note: Share of households that leave: 100% in Order zones, 50% in Warning zones, 20% shadow/voluntary elsewhere (Time Study 2-3, 7-1, from NUREG/CR-7002) (SOURCE_NOTES E8). Shadow evacuees drive to the city edge.

demand.childPickupShare.note: Share of households that pick up children when school is in session (switches to Time Study distributions E/F). Placeholder; ACS households with children would replace it.

demand.mobilization15min.note: Percent of trips starting in each 15-minute period after the order, Time Study Table 5-9 (p. 5-14) (SOURCE_NOTES E9). A employees/visitors; C residents awaiting a returning commuter (also used for shadow evacuees); D residents not awaiting one; E/F = C/D with child pickup.
